newsitem.title: JORDAN: Netanyahu put law in hands of settlers, PLO says.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu put law in hands of settlers, PLO says.

text.p: Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat blamed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday for recent clashes between Israelis and Palestinians, saying he encouraged Jewish settlers to take the law into their hands.
Erekat, speaking after talks with Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali, said Netanyahu had given settlers the go-ahead to seize more land from Palestinians.

"The Israeli settler can now expand his settlement, open a ring road or move the settlement boundaries... The law is in the hands of the Israeli settler, with Netanyahu's encouragement," Erekat told reporters.
"That will lead to more confrontations and the responsibility lies with Netanyahu, who gave the settlers the green light to take the law into their own hands," he added.
Israeli soldiers shot and wounded two Palestinians on Thursday during a clash with hundreds of Palestinians who planted olive trees on land seized by settlers.
Netanyahu blamed the clashes on the Palestinian Authority.
"There was a clear set of instructions a few days ago in Gaza for the violence that took place there," he said this week.
A gloomy Erekat said he welcomed Egyptian efforts to push forward stalled Israeli-Palestinian talks, but added that relations with Israel were still "in crisis".
"(The Egyptian moves) have not lifted the ceilings of expectations or the ceilings of optimism," he said.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, whose country is leading attempts to revive substantive talks between Israel and the Palestinians, said on Tuesday that a gap remained between the Israelis and the Palestinians and that the main obstacle to progress was still Israel's settlement policies.
Israeli-Palestinian talks have been deadlocked since the Israeli government decided in March to go ahead with a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
The Palestinians say the settlement breaks international law and preempts talks on the final status of Jerusalem and the Palestinian territories. Israel refuses to stop building settlements.
"It has become clear (Netanyahu) has a studied plan which in the end is targetted against the peace process," Erekat said.
